scope: R136 independent combined source review, exact Oracle candidate gates, and completed physical-router correctness gates; no performance or deployment verdict

review.decision: No blocking correctness defect found in the reviewed combined runtime diff; scoped evidence does not prove absence of every bug.
review.entry_and_id_collisions: Random occupied IDs retry without incrementing a type reference; fixed occupied IDs return AlreadyExists before mutation. Vacant insertion takes exactly one type reference. new_type retains methods until a vacant entry; no existing object/type is overwritten.
review.type_reference_lifetime: Temporary ADD reference is released after create, failed publication destroys the object and its reference, and destroy removes the type only after its last reference. Occupied-entry removal preserves the previous zero-count condition.
review.borrowed_path: cstr_bytes and ACL/duplicate checks precede Rc allocation. Rc<[u8]>::from copies before the received buffer can be reused; the map and object own cloned Rc handles. Event dispatch clones Rc before mutating server state. Existing set_path valid-object/single-bind precondition remains unchanged.
review.strings_and_wire: Object-event method names are fixed NUL-free bytes. The only runtime set_path caller canonicalizes at the first NUL, so msg_string_bytes truncation cannot change a stored path. Both new writers append one terminator and retain raw non-UTF8 bytes; type/header/padding/nesting are unchanged.
not_claimed: Forced random-ID collisions were structurally reviewed, not fault-injected.
Reference counter overflow behavior is pre-existing and unchanged.
Passing wire cases are a finite corpus, not exhaustive behavioral equivalence.
